threads.thread_goal: Align on campaign objectives, audiences and key messages before content creation.

messages.text:
Kicking off the awareness campaign work for project_pack_ref: Launch of Corporate Safety & Sustainability Awareness Campaign.
I have a first pass at objectives and audience groups for A1, plus a rough outline for the key messages that will feed into T1 and T11.
Draft objectives:
- Reinforce everyday safety and security behaviours across all sites
- Make it clear how each role contributes to a safer, more sustainable workplace
- Reduce avoidable incidents linked to lack of awareness
- Highlight simple sustainability actions people can take on shift
Primary audiences I am proposing:
- Frontline operations staff on sites
- Supervisors and site managers
- Office-based staff
- Contractors and temporary staff
Before I lock this into A1, can you all react and flag what feels off or missing? In particular, I want to be sure this lines up with the channel and strategy work in T2.

Thanks for sharing this early.
From a T2 perspective, the audience split makes sense to me. For the objectives, should we also call out something around consistent messages across sites and channels? That will help when we map channels and frequency in A1 and later in the content kit.
On the key messages for T1, can you share a short list of the top 5–7 points you are thinking of so we can test them against each audience?

From a quality and compliance angle, I like that the objectives focus on everyday behaviours.
Two points to consider before we freeze this in A1:
- We should explicitly mention alignment with existing safety and security procedures, so that T1 and T11 do not accidentally introduce new rules.
- For contractors and temporary staff, we may need simpler language and very clear do and do not examples.
If we agree, I can reflect these in the checklist draft for A2 later, but they should already appear in the objectives and key messages.

Looking at this with the launch events in mind, I would add one more objective: encourage people to speak up about safety and sustainability issues.
That will help us design interactive elements for events and on-site activations, and it ties well to the feedback loops we will need later.
For audiences, do we want to treat shift leaders separately from site managers, or keep them under supervisors and site managers for now?

From what I have seen on sites, people often miss basics like where to report a security concern or how to handle blocked exits.
For T1 and T11, I suggest we keep messages very concrete, like: know your nearest emergency exit, do not prop fire doors open, report suspicious behaviour to security using the site number.
I agree with adding something about following existing procedures. We should also avoid sharing any sensitive incident details when we collect examples for T11, so I will check with security management on that.

Here is a first cut of core messages for T1, grouped roughly by theme:
Safety and security:
- Follow site procedures and instructions from supervisors and security.
- Know how to report a concern or incident quickly.
- Keep exits, equipment and walkways clear.
Sustainability:
- Reduce waste where you can, including energy and materials.
- Use the right bins and follow local recycling rules.
Culture:
- Everyone has a role in keeping the workplace safe and sustainable.
- Speaking up early prevents bigger problems.
We can refine wording, but does this cover the essentials for A1?

This is a good base.
For T2, I will need to translate these into slightly different angles per audience. For example, for supervisors we might stress role-modelling and briefing teams, while for frontline staff we keep it very action oriented.
One question: do we want a separate message about data or information security, or is that out of scope for this campaign? If it is in scope, we should add a simple line to the security part before we finalise A1.

If we touch on information security, we need to be careful not to conflict with any existing policies or training.
I suggest we keep it high level in A1 and T1, something like: protect company and customer information, follow existing guidelines for passwords and devices.
We will then ask the security management team to review the detailed wording as part of T11 and the checklist in A2.

Agree we should keep information security simple.
When I collect scenarios for T11, I can focus on everyday examples like not sharing badges, locking screens, and not letting unknown visitors tailgate into restricted areas.
I will avoid anything that could reveal sensitive procedures and will ask security management to confirm the final list.

For events, it would help if A1 also includes one or two emotional hooks, not just instructions.
For example, linking safety to going home safe every day, and sustainability to leaving a better workplace for colleagues and communities.
That will make it easier to design interactive moments and stories during launch sessions.

On the audience list, I propose we keep shift leaders under supervisors and site managers for now, but in T2 I will call them out explicitly when we define channels and frequency.
So the final audience groups in A1 would be:
- Frontline operations staff
- Supervisors, shift leaders and site managers
- Office-based staff
- Contractors and temporary staff
If no one objects, I will use this structure in the strategy draft.

Works for me.
Let me try to summarise the updated objectives and audiences for A1 based on this thread:
Objectives:
- Reinforce everyday safety and security behaviours across all sites.
- Make it clear how each role contributes to a safer, more sustainable workplace.
- Reduce avoidable incidents linked to lack of awareness.
- Highlight simple sustainability actions people can take on shift.
- Encourage people to speak up about safety, security and sustainability issues.
- Ensure messages are consistent with existing procedures and policies.
Audiences:
- Frontline operations staff.
- Supervisors, shift leaders and site managers.
- Office-based staff.
- Contractors and temporary staff.
If you are comfortable with this, we can treat this as the final list for A1 and T2.

The summary looks good to me and gives enough clarity for downstream work.
From my side, I am fine to treat this as the agreed set of objectives and audience segments for A1 and for planning in T2.
I will reference these in the quality checklist so we can check that assets stay aligned.

No objections from me.
This gives us a clear frame for event concepts in T3 and for how we brief local champions.
I will make sure our event formats support the speak up objective and give space for questions on safety and sustainability.

I am also aligned with these objectives and audiences.
For T1 and T11, I will keep the examples practical and tied to existing procedures, and I will avoid technical language so contractors and temporary staff can follow easily.

Next step is to lock the core messages into A1 so others can start using them.
Based on feedback, I will:
- Add a short line on information security, kept high level.
- Include an emotional hook for safety and sustainability.
- Keep language simple and action oriented.
Once I update A1, I will share a link here and mark it as ready for use in T1, T2 and T11.

I have now updated A1 with the refined objectives, audiences and the core message set we discussed.
Unless there are strong objections today, I suggest we treat these key messages as signed off so that T1 can move into drafting detailed copy and T2 can finalise the strategy.
Please react here if you are ok with that.

I have reviewed the latest A1 draft.
The objectives and key messages are consistent with current safety and security procedures and use accessible language.
From my side, I am comfortable treating the core messages in A1 as approved for use in T1, T2 and T11.

Confirmed from my side as well.
I will now proceed with T2 using the approved objectives, audiences and key messages in A1, and I will mirror the wording in the content kit work later.

threads.thread_goal: Define the campaign channel mix, calendar and event concepts.

messages.text:
I have put together a first draft of the channel plan in A3, based on the agreed objectives and audiences in A1 and the early thinking for T5 and T7.
Proposed channel mix:
- Intranet news and banners for all staff.
- Targeted email updates for supervisors, shift leaders and office-based staff.
- Digital signage or screens where available on sites.
- Printed posters and quick-reference cards in high-traffic areas.
- Short segments in existing team briefings and toolbox talks.
For frequency, I am thinking of a 3-week push:
- Week 1: launch announcement and core messages.
- Week 2: focus on safety and security behaviours.
- Week 3: focus on sustainability and speak up culture.
For events (T3 and T8), I have left placeholders in A3 and would like input from you on formats and timing before we lock anything.
Feedback welcome on channels, frequency and any gaps.

Thanks for the draft.
On events for T3, I suggest we plan for three main formats across key sites:
- Short launch huddles during shift changes.
- One slightly longer town-hall style session at the largest site.
- Pop-up stands in canteens or entrance areas with quick demos and Q&A.
In A3, we could anchor these in week 1 and early week 2 so that the rest of the channel activity can reinforce what people hear at the events.
Does that fit with your calendar assumptions?

From a messaging standpoint, the 3-week structure works.
One concern: for contractors and temporary staff, intranet and email may not be enough.
Could we add:
- Briefing cards for site induction sessions.
- A simple one-page handout that supervisors can use during toolbox talks.
These would sit under T5 and T7 and be tracked in A3 as well.

On sites, people pay more attention to what is said in person than to emails.
For T7, I would focus posters and quick-reference cards near time clocks, canteens and locker rooms.
For T3 events, short huddles at the start of shifts will probably reach more frontline staff than a single big session.
We should also make sure any on-site signage matches the same instructions they already see in safety procedures.

From a review and logistics perspective, the proposed mix is manageable if we are clear on priorities.
I suggest we treat these as must-have channels in A3:
- Intranet.
- Team briefings and toolbox talks.
- On-site posters and quick-reference cards.
Email and digital signage can be nice-to-have where capacity allows.
This will help us keep T5, T7 and T8 realistic within the 21-day window and keep the review load in A6 under control.

The three event formats you propose fit well with the 3-week calendar.
In A3, I will tentatively place:
- Shift-change huddles in week 1 across the three key sites.
- One town-hall style session at the largest site in week 1.
- Pop-up stands in canteens in late week 1 and early week 2.
We will need to confirm dates and times with site operations as part of T3 and T8.
I will mark these as draft until you have had a chance to speak with the sites.

Sounds good.
I will reach out to the three key sites today to check availability for week 1 and early week 2 and will update T3 and T8 with confirmed dates, times and locations.
Once confirmed, we can lock those into A3 and start drafting the run-of-show in A5.

Good point on contractors and temporary staff.
I will add:
- Induction briefing cards.
- A one-page handout for toolbox talks.
These will be part of T5 and T7 and will be scheduled in A3 alongside the team briefings.
For frequency, I propose:
- At least one briefing per team during week 1.
- A short reminder in week 3 focused on sustainability and speak up.
Does that feel realistic for supervisors?

Yes, one main briefing in week 1 and a reminder in week 3 sounds workable.
We just need to keep the briefing cards short so they fit into existing toolbox talks.
If you share a draft from T5, I can check that the instructions match what people already hear in safety briefings.

To keep the review process smooth, I will set up A6 with separate tabs or views for:
- Digital content (intranet, email).
- On-site materials (posters, cards, stands).
- Event materials (slides, run-of-show in A5).
For each, we will track owner, reviewer and approver, and I will propose simple service expectations so we do not block the calendar in A3.
We can refine this in the quality thread, but I wanted to flag the dependency here.

Let me summarise the proposed channel mix and minimum frequency per audience so we can see if we are ready to confirm.
Frontline operations staff:
- Team briefings and toolbox talks: at least 1 main briefing in week 1 + 1 reminder in week 3.
- On-site posters and quick-reference cards in high-traffic areas: visible from week 1.
- Pop-up stands in canteens or entrances at key sites: during week 1 and early week 2.
Supervisors, shift leaders and site managers:
- Targeted email updates: 1 launch email in week 1 + 1 reminder in week 3.
- Briefing packs and induction cards to use with teams.
Office-based staff:
- Intranet news and banners: launch in week 1, follow-ups in weeks 2 and 3.
Contractors and temporary staff:
- Induction briefing cards and one-page handouts used at site entry and toolbox talks.
If we agree this is the baseline, I will mark it as the final channel mix and minimum frequency in A3.

This summary looks balanced and aligned with the objectives in A1.
From my side, I am comfortable treating this as the agreed channel mix and minimum frequency for planning and content development in T5 and T7.

Agreed on the channel mix and frequency.
On events, based on early checks with sites, I propose we confirm:
- Three key sites with launch activities.
- At each site: shift-change huddles plus a pop-up stand.
- One town-hall style session at the largest site.
Timing:
- All launch activities to happen in week 1, with pop-up stands extending into early week 2 if needed.
If everyone is ok, we can treat this as the agreed number, format and timing for events and I will reflect it in T3, T8, A3 and A5.

The proposed event scope is reasonable for the timeline and review capacity.
I am fine to confirm this as the agreed number, format and timing of internal launch events for A3 and A5.
We will just need to ensure that event materials go through the review flow in A6 with enough lead time.

I support the event plan.
For the shift-change huddles, we should keep the agenda tight so it fits into existing routines.
When you draft the run-of-show in A5, I can help check that the safety and security points are clear and match site procedures.

Great, thanks all.
I will now update A3 to reflect the confirmed channel mix, minimum frequency and event plan.
Next steps from my side:
- Finalise the channel calendar in A3.
- Start drafting the digital content kit for T5, aligned with A1.
- Coordinate with @178948 on any content needs for events in A5.
I will share a link to the updated A3 once done.

threads.thread_goal: Set up and validate the quality and compliance review process for all assets.

messages.text:
I have drafted the quality and compliance checklist in A2 and a first version of the review workflow for T4 and T9.
A2 currently covers:
- Legal and safety checks (alignment with existing procedures, no conflicting instructions).
- Security checks (no sensitive details, correct escalation paths).
- Brand and tone checks (aligned with A1, clear for non-specialists).
- Accessibility and language checks.
For the workflow in T9, I am proposing:
- Owner drafts asset and logs it in A6.
- Quality and safety review.
- Final approval by corporate communications or relevant lead.
Before we finalise, I would like your input on:
- Any missing checks for events and on-site signage.
- Reasonable review timelines so we do not block the calendar in A3.

Thanks for setting this up.
For digital content in T5 and on-site signage in T7, one extra check that might help is making sure calls to action are realistic for each audience.
For example, office staff can click links, but frontline staff may need a phone number or a person to contact.
On timelines, for standard assets like intranet posts and posters, would a 2-working-day review window work, assuming we plan ahead in A3?

For events in T3 and T8, I would add to A2:
- A quick check that the event format itself does not create safety issues (for example, no blocking of exits with stands).
- A check that any live demos follow site safety rules.
On timelines, event materials like the run-of-show in A5 and any slides probably need a slightly longer window, maybe 3 working days, because they involve more stakeholders.

On the safety and security side, I suggest A2 also checks that:
- Emergency contacts and reporting channels are correct for each site.
- We do not show any restricted areas or sensitive equipment in photos.
For T1 and T11, I can help review scenarios to make sure they are realistic and do not reveal too much about security procedures, but final sign-off should come from security management.

From a spokesperson and messaging angle, I would add a consistency check in A2:
- Does the asset reflect the approved objectives, audiences and key messages in A1?
This will help us avoid drift as different people work on T5, T6, T7 and T12.
On the workflow in T9, it would be helpful if A6 clearly shows where an asset is waiting, so we can nudge reviewers if needed.

These are helpful additions.
I will update A2 to include:
- Audience-appropriate calls to action.
- Event safety checks.
- Correct contacts and no sensitive visuals.
- Alignment with A1.
On timelines, I propose we standardise as follows for T9 and A6:
- Standard assets (intranet posts, posters, briefing cards): 2 working days for review.
- Event materials (A5, slides): 3 working days.
- Critical corrections (for example, fixing an error in a live asset): same day where possible.
If this sounds reasonable, we can treat these as our default expectations.

The proposed timelines work for me.
For T5 and T7, I will plan content creation in A3 so that we always have at least 2 working days before the planned go-live date.
It would be useful if A6 could flag any assets that are at risk of missing their slot so we can adjust the calendar or simplify the asset.

I am comfortable with the 3-day window for event materials.
For T3 and T8, I will aim to have draft run-of-show documents in A5 and any slides ready at least 4 working days before the event, so there is time for review and any fixes.
Please just confirm in A6 who the final approver is for event content so I know who to loop in.

For event materials, I propose the following sign-off chain in A6 and T9:
- Owner: event manager.
- Reviewers: safety officer for the site, quality services.
- Final approver: corporate communications representative.
For digital and print assets, the owner will be the person leading T5 or T7, with similar reviewer and approver roles.
I will document this in A6 so it is clear for everyone.

The review windows look ok.
For T1, T6, T11 and T12, I will plan drafts so that security management has enough time to look at the scenarios and Q&A.
Please include a note in A2 that any changes requested by security or safety officers override our drafts, so we do not accidentally keep outdated instructions.

I support the checklist updates and the proposed timelines.
For spokesperson materials in A4 and A8, it would help if A2 also checks that:
- We do not promise anything operational teams cannot deliver.
- We clearly state where employees can find more information.
If you add that, I am happy to work with you on the first couple of reviews so we can calibrate how we apply the checklist.

I have now incorporated all the suggestions into A2 and updated the workflow and roles in A6 for T4 and T9.
To recap the key points:
- A2 covers legal, safety, security, brand, accessibility, audience fit, event safety and alignment with A1.
- A6 tracks owner, reviewers, approver and status for each asset.
- Standard review windows: 2 working days for standard assets, 3 for event materials, with same-day corrections where needed.
Unless there are strong objections, I propose we treat this version of A2 as our final checklist for the campaign.

Confirmed from my side.
I will use A2 and A6 as the reference for all assets coming out of T5 and T7.
The review windows and roles are clear enough for planning.

I am aligned as well.
For T3 and T8, I will log all event-related materials in A6 and route them through the A2 checklist with the 3-day window.
This should give us enough time to fix any issues before events.

No objections.
I will follow A2 and A6 for spokesperson materials in A4 and A8 and will coordinate with you on the first reviews.
This should help keep messages consistent and compliant across channels.

One last point to close: for T9, I propose we formalise the review expectations as follows and record them in A6:
- Owners log assets in A6 at least 2 or 3 working days before planned go-live, depending on type.
- Reviewers aim to respond within the agreed window; if they cannot, they flag it in the channel.
- Final approvers confirm or request changes within 1 working day after review.
If everyone is ok, we can treat these as our agreed review service expectations for the campaign.

Agreed on these expectations.
I will plan T5 and T7 timelines accordingly and will flag in the channel if we see any risk of missing a slot in A3.

threads.thread_goal: Align on spokesperson materials, manager briefing guide and FAQs.

messages.text:
I have drafted initial versions of the spokesperson talking points and Q&A in A4 and the manager briefing guide and FAQ in A8, based on A1 and the scenarios we plan for T6 and T12.
Highlights:
- A4: short opening script for launch events, 5 key talking points, and a Q&A covering common questions on safety, security, sustainability and what changes for employees.
- A8: a 2-page manager briefing guide with a simple structure (why this campaign, what to say, what to do) and an FAQ for employees.
Before we move to sign-off, I would like your feedback on:
- Any missing questions or concerns we should address.
- Whether the tone and level of detail work for frontline staff and managers.
- Any operational promises that feel risky or unrealistic.

Looking at A4, the talking points are clear.
For the Q&A, I suggest we add:
- A question on what to do if someone sees a blocked exit or unsafe behaviour.
- A question on how to report suspicious people or items.
For A8, maybe include a short checklist for managers to walk around their area and spot obvious safety or sustainability issues before they brief their teams.
I will also send the Q&A part of T6 and T12 to security management for a quick check on the security-related answers.

For events in T3, the opening script in A4 is a good length.
I would suggest adding one short interactive element, such as asking people to share one safety or sustainability action they already take.
For A8, it might help managers if we include a suggested 10-minute agenda they can use in team briefings, so they know how to fit this into existing meetings.

From a channel and content perspective, the tone in A4 and A8 feels consistent with A1.
One thing to watch: in the FAQ, we should be careful not to promise new equipment or major changes unless operations has confirmed them.
Maybe we can rephrase some answers to focus on behaviours and awareness rather than new investments.
Also, could we add a short section in A8 on how managers can use the digital content from T5 in their briefings?

I have checked A4 and A8 against A2.
Overall they align well, but I recommend a few tweaks:
- Make sure all references to procedures match current safety and security guidance.
- Add a clear pointer in A8 to where employees can find more information (for example, intranet page or local noticeboard).
- Avoid any language that could be read as a guarantee of zero incidents.
Once we incorporate these, I will be comfortable recommending sign-off.

Thanks for the suggestions.
I will update A4 to include Q&A items on blocked exits, unsafe behaviour and reporting suspicious people or items, and I will keep the answers aligned with existing procedures.
For A8, I like the idea of a simple walk-around checklist and a 10-minute agenda; I will add both so managers have something concrete to use.
Once you have feedback from security management on T6 and T12, please let me know if we need to adjust any wording.

Good call on not over-promising.
I will review the FAQ in A8 and rephrase any answers that suggest new equipment or major changes, focusing instead on behaviours, awareness and how to use existing channels.
I will also add a short note for managers on how to bring in digital content from T5, such as showing intranet posts or using email snippets in briefings.

I have now applied the checklist feedback from A2 to A4 and A8:
- Checked procedure references with the latest safety and security guidance.
- Added a clear pointer to the intranet page and local noticeboards for more information.
- Removed any wording that could sound like a guarantee of zero incidents.
I have also integrated the interactive element for events and the manager agenda.
Could you please do a quick second pass and confirm if A4 is ready for sign-off?

I have rechecked A4 against A2.
The talking points and Q&A now:
- Align with approved messages in A1.
- Reflect current safety and security procedures.
- Use clear, accessible language.
From my side, I am comfortable treating A4 as ready for use in T6 and for event hosts.
If others agree, we can mark the spokesperson talking points and Q&A pack as approved.

I have reviewed A4 from an event flow perspective.
The script length and Q&A structure work well for T3, and the interactive element should help engagement.
I am fine to use A4 as the standard pack for event hosts.

Security management has reviewed the Q&A sections related to security and is ok with the current wording in A4.
From my side, I am comfortable using this pack for T6 and for answering questions during events and briefings.

Thanks all.
I will treat A4 as approved and will share it with designated spokespeople and event hosts as part of T6.
Next, I would like to close on A8.
With the latest updates, A8 now includes:
- A simple explanation of the campaign purpose and timing.
- A 10-minute agenda for team briefings.
- A short walk-around checklist.
- An FAQ focused on behaviours and existing channels, with clear pointers to more information.
Are you comfortable approving A8 for distribution to managers and HR?

I have reviewed the latest A8 draft.
The structure is clear and should be easy for managers to use.
From my side, I am fine to approve A8 for distribution, and I will reference it in T5 communications so managers know where to find it.

I have checked A8 against A2.
It meets the checklist criteria and does not introduce any conflicting instructions.
I support approving A8 for use by managers and HR as part of T12.

I am also ok with A8.
The guidance is practical and does not promise changes that operations has not confirmed.
I will use it when briefing managers and will share any questions we hear back so we can update the FAQ later if needed.

Great, thanks for the reviews.
I will now:
- Share A4 with all designated spokespeople and event hosts and log this under T6.
- Coordinate with HR and internal communications to upload A8 to the intranet and send it to managers as part of T12.
We can adjust both documents later if we see recurring questions during the campaign.

threads.thread_goal: Review launch readiness and define post-campaign measurement approach.

messages.text:
Ahead of launch, I have updated A6 with the latest asset statuses and run the pre-launch checks using A2.
Summary:
- Core messaging in A1 is approved.
- Channel calendar in A3 is populated for the 3-week push.
- Most digital and print assets are created and either approved or in final review.
- Event plans in A5 are drafted and under review.
Remaining gaps:
- A small number of site-specific posters are still in review.
- One event run-of-show is waiting for final confirmation from operations.
I would like to:
1) Confirm whether we are comfortable giving a go for launch with these minor items still in progress.
2) Align on the measurement framework in T10 and how we will use A7 for the post-campaign evaluation.
Please share any concerns that would prevent you from supporting a go decision.

From a channel and content side, I am comfortable with launch as long as:
- The remaining posters in review do not block critical safety messages at any site.
- We have at least one approved asset per key channel listed in A3 for week 1.
Based on A6, this seems to be the case.
For measurement in T10, I propose we track:
- Reach: intranet views, email open rates, number of briefings held.
- Engagement: clicks on intranet content, questions asked at events, feedback forms.
- Early signals: any reported changes in incident types that are clearly linked to awareness.
We can structure these in A7 for the evaluation report.

On events, A5 shows that two of the three key site run-of-show documents are fully approved.
The remaining one is only waiting for a final time confirmation from operations, not for content changes.
From my perspective, this is not a blocker for the overall campaign launch, as long as we do not communicate the exact time for that event until it is confirmed.
For measurement, we can also track event attendance and a quick pulse question at the end of each session, such as: do you feel clearer about what is expected of you?

From a safety and security angle, I have checked the remaining posters in A6.
They are site-specific variations of already approved designs, and the core instructions are the same.
As long as we do not put up any unapproved versions, I do not see a reason to delay launch.
For measurement, we might also look at whether reporting of near-misses or unsafe conditions increases in the short term, which could show that people are more willing to speak up.

I am comfortable with launch, provided we:
- Clearly mark in A6 which assets are approved and which are still pending, and avoid using pending ones.
- Brief spokespeople and managers using A4 and A8 before the first events and briefings.
On measurement for T10 and A7, I suggest we also capture qualitative feedback from managers and employees, for example:
- Short comments from managers after briefings.
- A simple feedback form on the intranet page.
These will help us understand not just what people saw, but what they took away.

Thanks for the inputs.
On readiness:
- A6 confirms that each key channel in A3 has at least one approved asset for week 1.
- Remaining posters are variants of approved designs and will not be used until they pass A2.
- Event content in A5 is approved for two sites and content-complete for the third.
Given this, I am inclined to recommend a go for launch, with a note that we will monitor closely in the first days.
On measurement, combining your suggestions, I propose the following framework for T10 and A7:
- Reach: intranet views, email opens, number of briefings and events, attendance.
- Engagement: clicks, questions at events, feedback forms, pulse questions.
- Behaviour signals: changes in reporting of near-misses and unsafe conditions, any early shifts in incident patterns.
- Qualitative feedback: comments from managers and employees.
If you agree, I will document this in A7 and T10.

I support both the go recommendation and the measurement framework.
I will make sure the intranet and email assets include links to the feedback form and that we can pull basic reach and engagement data for A7.
No further concerns from my side.

I am aligned with the go decision.
For events, I will:
- Confirm the remaining time slot with operations.
- Capture attendance numbers and pulse question responses.
I will feed these into A7 so they can be reflected in the evaluation report.

I also support launching now.
I will remind security and safety officers at key sites to watch for any confusion or issues in the first week and to share quick feedback.
For the behaviour signals in T10, I can help collect data on near-miss and unsafe condition reports so we can compare before and after the campaign.

I am comfortable with the go decision and the measurement approach.
I will brief spokespeople and managers using A4 and A8 before the first events and team briefings, and I will encourage them to capture any recurring questions so we can include them in the evaluation using A7.

Thanks everyone.
Based on the checks in A2 and A6 and your feedback, we will proceed with launch.
I will:
- Mark the campaign as go in A6 and notify corporate communications.
- Finalise the measurement framework in T10 and complete the A7 template with the agreed KPIs, data sources and feedback channels.
We will aim to produce the post-campaign evaluation report using A7 within two weeks after the 3-week push ends.
